summary: Fix a cross-platform CRLF defect in the CLI's frontmatter parser so doctor recognizes schema_version frontmatter on Windows checkouts, and normalize tracked text artifacts to LF so git autocrlf stops reintroducing the problem.
goals: doctor passes on a fresh Windows checkout instead of falsely reporting frontmatter as missing.
parseFrontmatter tolerates both LF and CRLF line endings at the frontmatter delimiter.
Prevent regressions by normalizing markdown/JSON artifacts to LF via .gitattributes and covering the parser with a test.

features.name: CRLF-tolerant frontmatter parsing
features.description: parseFrontmatter accepts a leading CRLF ('---' then carriage-return newline) as well as a bare LF so frontmatter artifacts validate regardless of line endings.

features.name: Line-ending normalization
features.description: A .gitattributes normalizes tracked text artifacts (.md/.json) to LF in the repo so git autocrlf does not rewrite them to CRLF on Windows checkout.

features.name: Regression test
features.description: A test asserts parseFrontmatter reads schema_version from CRLF-terminated frontmatter.

constraints: No behavior change beyond line-ending tolerance; the CLI stays deterministic and zero-dependency.
Do not alter the frontmatter schema or any artifact contents.
